synthesis: The initial w=1 residue separates into a holomorphic Euler remainder whose central value is the arithmetic factor and universal zeta diagonals. The zero-frequency stabilizer transports that principal part across the reflected polar arrangement; under Conjecture 2.7, orbit symmetrization and homogeneous divisibility cancellation select the pole order and geometric factor, after which Wiener-Ikehara transfer gives the even zeta-moment asymptotic.

Propositions 2.6 and Conjecture 2.7 identify the zero-frequency reflection orbit of that pole and posit that it is the complete local divisor. Theorem 2.8 reduces the moment to the leading Laurent coefficient, while Proposition 2.9 and Lemma 2.10 evaluate the orbit model by common-denominator divisibility and homogeneous scaling, leaving the constant Taylor term and g_{2m}.

limits: The moment conclusion depends on the continuation, local-divisor completeness, and central holomorphy asserted in Conjecture 2.7; the orbit calculation alone does not establish those hypotheses. If Conjecture 3.6 identifies the full reflected local divisor, orbit divisibility and scaling supply the geometric factor and the Tauberian step yields the even-moment asymptotic.

Conjecture 3.6 and Theorem 3.7 state the required polar completeness and conditional Tauberian implication, while Proposition 3.8 and Lemmas 3.9-3.10 evaluate the reflected principal-part orbit by divisibility and homogeneous reduction to its constant term.

limits: The all-m conclusion is conditional on every analytic assertion in Conjecture 3.6, and the stated Tauberian theorem applies to even m. Their finite dihedral action, together with pole clearing and successive tube convex hulls, gives global continuation and vertical control for corrected building blocks. Finite local identities, two Möbius stages, and character combinations then reconstruct the fundamental-discriminant series; a shifted three-variable residue calculation fixes the seventh-order leading term, and contour inversion produces the cubic moment polynomial.

Propositions 4.2-4.3 give the two vector functional equations; Propositions 4.8-4.10 turn their D12 action into staged continuation to C^2 after clearing stated poles, and Propositions 4.11-4.12 provide finite-order and vertical-strip control. nonparaphrase_operation: Assembles the proof as a sequence of interfaces: canonical local completion closes dual summation equations, finite reflection geometry propagates analyticity, arithmetic projectors recover primitive discriminants, and shifted residue data feed Mellin-contour extraction.
limits: This architecture is specialized to the GL(3) Eisenstein realization of the cubic family and does not extend automatically to the nonunique, infinite-group higher-degree setting.
